blocks.text: Why economists need a better Chrome workflow

The modern economist does not just read papers. You clean data, run regressions, and manage bibliographies. Your browser is where this starts. You likely have dozens of tabs open for different projects. This creates a cognitive load that slows down your deep work. Using Chrome effectively on macOS requires more than just installing extensions. It requires a system for managing your digital environment.

Stop clicking the back button. Use ⌘ + [ to go back and ⌘ + ] to go forward. Use ⌘ + T for a new tab and ⌘ + W to close the current one. If you accidentally close a tab, hit ⌘ + ⇧ + T to reopen it instantly. These small movements add up over a day of research.

blocks.text: Organize your research with Chrome profiles

Do not mix your teaching materials with your primary research data. Create a dedicated Chrome profile for each major project. This keeps your cookies, extensions, and bookmarks isolated. Go to the profile icon in the top right, click Add, and set up a new environment. This prevents your browsing history from becoming a cluttered mess.

Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you are looking at a complex data table on a government website, ask Lazur to summarize the trends. It reads your screen and speaks the answer back to you. This saves you from manually copying and pasting text into a separate AI tool.
Ask Lazur to research a specific topic while you work on your Stata code. Lazur runs the search in its own background tabs and provides a report when finished.
blocks.title: Background research

blocks.text: Too many extensions will crash your browser during a large data pull. Review your extensions by typing chrome://extensions in your address bar. Disable anything you have not used in the last month. For researchers, keep a lean setup. Use only what is necessary for citation management or academic database access.
Clearing site data for cleaner results

Sometimes a website will not load correctly because of stale cache. Instead of clearing everything, clear data for that specific site. Click the lock icon in the address bar, then Site settings. From there, you can clear data for that domain without logging yourself out of every other site you use.

Economists often find that digital tools raise the bar for expected output. You run a regression faster, so you are expected to run ten more. Use Lazur to dictate notes into your research diary or to quickly set reminders for upcoming submission deadlines. This keeps your administrative tasks from eating into your research time.

If you use Zotero, ensure the browser connector is pinned to your toolbar. Clicking the icon saves the metadata immediately. If the connector fails, use the print function to save the page as a PDF for offline review. Keeping your literature organized is the first step toward a successful paper.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons on websites for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides you or points at things, but it does not interact with the web page directly. You remain in control of every click.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my browsing history?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only looks at your screen while you hold the activation key. It does not store your history or personal data on its servers.

faq.question: How do I speed up Chrome if it feels slow?
faq.answer: Clear your cache, remove unused extensions, and ensure you are not running too many tabs at once. Using separate profiles for different projects also helps.
